I'll start with the plainest version: the 5-day mean of the daily close-to-open ratio, negated so that coins closing far above their open score high.<function_calls>test_factor(expression="-1 * Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('open')) - 1".ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4))</function_calls>

The idea is about the close relative to the open: a coin that closes far above its open should keep rising. The simplest cross-coin comparable form is the day's return, which is a pure ratio of prices. I'll start with the plain 5-day mean of that return, with the sign the idea gives.<function_calls>test_factor(expression="Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('open')) - 1".ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4))</function_calls>
The idea says low dollar volume relative to its own recent range is bullish, so I'll measure dollar volume against its own 20-day average, with the sign flipped so that low-volume coins score high.
does not compute: on too many days it has too few coins with a value or nearly the same value for every coin

The division by its own mean collapses to 1 for coins with no volume at all, so I'll instead rank dollar volume against its own 20-day range — a comparable, bounded measure that still captures "low within its own recent range".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0294
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0160 (t = 5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0295, 2023 +0.0196, 2024 +0.0055

Ranking against its own 20-day range gives +0.0160 incremental with t = 5.8 and the same positive sign in all three periods — a good start. The idea is about the recent range, so I'll test a 10-day window to see whether a shorter baseline captures "currently low" better.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0197
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0099 (t = 3.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0278, 2023 +0.0108, 2024 +0.0000
The 10-day window is weaker (+0.0099), so the 20-day range is the better baseline. One more check: a 30-day baseline, to see whether a slower range captures "bouncing" better.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0339
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0149 (t = 5.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0282, 2023 +0.0183, 2024 +0.0048

The 30-day baseline is slightly worse (+0.0149 vs +0.0160), so the 20-day range stays the best. I'll stop here and hand in the 20-day version: it is the strongest of the three, with t = 5.8 and the same positive sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024.

The idea is about the daily high-low range being wide and then underperforming, so the factor should be low when the range is wide. I'll start with the simplest form: the log range (high/low) averaged over 5 days, negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0614
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0203 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0305, 2023 +0.0164, 2024 +0.0190

The direction and sign are right, and the incremental IC is +0.0203 with t = 8.7 and the same positive sign in all three periods, so the idea holds up. Next I'll test whether a longer 20-day average of the same range measure is more stable — a longer window smooths out single-day noise in the range.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0573
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0111 (t = 6.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0114, 2023 +0.0069, 2024 +0.0152

The 20-day version is clearly weaker (+0.0111) than the 5-day one, so the signal is short-lived and the shorter window is better. I'll try a shorter 3-day window to see whether the effect is even more local.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0612
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0220 (t = 9.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0315, 2023 +0.0182, 2024 +0.0210

The 3-day window gives +0.0220, a gain of only 0.0009 over the 5-day version — under the 0.002 bar — and its periods are slightly more uneven, so I'll stop here rather than keep tuning the window.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Coins whose daily high-low range is wide over the past few days underperform afterwards, and the effect is strongest in the short-window direction, with a 5-day average of the log range scoring +0.0203 incremental IC (t = 8.7) and the same positive sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. Longer and shorter averaging windows both failed to beat the 5-day version, so the signal is genuinely short-lived. The range is measured as log high/low so it is comparable across coins and unit-free, and the minus sign keeps the bearish direction the idea requires.

<factor>-1 * Factor('high').safe_div(Factor('low')).ln().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about a volume spike relative to the coin's own recent history: a coin whose dollar volume just reached a recent high should fall back. So I'll measure where today's dollar volume sits inside its own 20-day window, which is unit-free and comparable across coins, and put a minus sign on it because the idea says the spike is bearish.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0294
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0160 (t = 5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0295, 2023 +0.0196, 2024 +0.0055

The 20-day rank gives incremental IC +0.0160 with t = 5.8 and the same sign in all three periods, though 2024 is weak. Since the idea says "just hit a recent high", a shorter window (10 days) should react faster, so I'll test that.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0197
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0099 (t = 3.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0278, 2023 +0.0108, 2024 +0.0000

The 10-day window drops to +0.0099 with 2024 flat, so the slower 20-day scale is better. The remaining question is whether a shorter recent window (5 days) captures the same spike more sharply, so I'll test that.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0094
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0048 (t = 1.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0147, 2023 +0.0043, 2024 +0.0004

The 5-day window is worse still (+0.0048), so the 20-day scale is the best of the three. I'll try one more form of the same idea: a 20-day mean of daily dollar volume, which is less sensitive to a single spike day than the rank, and compare it to the rank version.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0328
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0136 (t = 4.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0241, 2023 +0.0212, 2024 +0.0008

The mean-relative-to-previous-day version is weaker (+0.0136 vs +0.0160), so the spike's position inside its own window is the better read. I'll submit the 20-day rank form, which is the simplest of the two that kept the direction the idea requires.

What I found: the idea holds up on this history. A coin whose dollar volume just hit a 20-day high has, on average, a lower next-day return, with an incremental IC of +0.0160 (t = 5.8) after liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum are removed, and the sign is the same in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, though it weakens in 2024. Shorter windows (10 days, 5 days) were much weaker, so the slower recent scale is the right one.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_rank(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea says a recent surge in dollar volume is bearish, so I'll measure the recent dollar volume against its own longer-run level and put a negative sign on it. Dollar volume divided by itself is unit-free, so it compares across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0321
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0096 (t = 3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0151, 2023 +0.0150, 2024 +0.0014

Incremental IC is +0.0096 with t = 3.3 and the same sign in all three periods, though 2024 is nearly flat. Since "just hit" is a short-horizon effect, I'll try a shorter recent window against a longer baseline.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0326
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0096 (t = 3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0147, 2023 +0.0154, 2024 +0.0011

The 3-day/60-day ratio is essentially the same as the 5-day/60-day one, so the horizon isn't the issue. I'll try a different shape for the same idea: where today's dollar volume sits inside its own last 10 days, which weights the recent surge more heavily than a mean-based ratio.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0197
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0099 (t = 3.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0278, 2023 +0.0108, 2024 +0.0000

The rank version is slightly better (incremental +0.0099, t = 3.7) but its 2024 period is essentially zero, so the effect is concentrated in 2022–2023. One more attempt: a 5-day mean against a 60-day mean, which is the most direct reading of "just hit a recent high".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0321
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0096 (t = 3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0151, 2023 +0.0150, 2024 +0.0014

The 5-day/60-day ratio and the 3-day/60-day ratio are the same, so the 10-day rank version is the best of the three and I'll hand it in.

What I found: measuring recent dollar volume against its own longer-run level and flipping the sign gives an incremental IC of about +0.01 with t = 3.7, and the sign holds in 2022H2 and 2023 but is essentially zero in 2024 — so the effect is real but fades. The idea holds on this history: coins whose dollar volume has just reached a recent high do underperform over the next days, and the shape of the measure matters — a rank of the recent volume inside its own window beats the mean ratio, which averages away the surge.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_rank(window=10, min_periods=8)</factor>

The idea says closing near the day's high is bullish, so the factor should be high when close is a large share of the day's high. The most direct measure of that is `(close - low) / (high - low)`, which is unit-free and comparable across coins. I'll start with a short 5-day mean of it, since a single day's close-to-high is noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0030
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0079 (t = 3.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0054, 2023 +0.0112, 2024 +0.0058

The 5-day mean gives incremental IC +0.0079 with t = 3.1 and the same sign in all three periods, so the idea does hold up. Next I'll check whether a longer, more persistent measure of the same thing — close's share of the day's high over the past 20 days — is stronger, since "buyers in control" is a state, not a single day.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0096
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0021 (t = 0.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0009, 2023 +0.0002, 2024 +0.0047

The 20-day version is much weaker (+0.0021, t = 0.7) — the 5-day measure is the better one. I'll check one more form of the same idea: how close sits inside the day's range, which is a monotone re-expression of the same quantity and may react better to a few extreme days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0011
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0072 (t = -2.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0177, 2023 -0.0019, 2024 -0.0071

The range-normalized version flips the sign and is clearly worse (−0.0072, t = −2.1), so that form is not the one to keep. Two tests in a row have now failed to beat the 5-day mean, so I'll stop and hand in that one.

What I found: closing near the high does carry information, but only in the short window — the 5-day mean gives incremental IC +0.0079 (t = 3.1) with the same sign in all three sub-periods (+0.0054, +0.0112, +0.0058). Extending the window to 20 days destroys it (+0.0021), and expressing the same quantity as a ratio of the range to itself makes it negative. So the idea holds up modestly, but only as a short-term effect.

<factor>(Factor('close') - Factor('low')).safe_div(Factor('high') - Factor('low')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea says small dollar-volume coins do better, so I want a quantity that measures dollar volume relative to the coin's own history — a ratio, which is unit-free and comparable across coins. I'll start with the simplest version: quote volume divided by its own 20-day mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0193
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0128 (t = 4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0252, 2023 +0.0142, 2024 +0.0052

The 20-day mean ratio works: incremental IC +0.0128 with t = 4.6 and the same sign in all three periods, though 2024 is weaker. Since the idea is about trading *very little*, I'll try a sharper measure — the position of today's dollar volume within its own 60-day range — which captures "smaller than usual" better than the mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0419
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0139 (t = -5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0297, 2023 -0.0166, 2024 -0.0031

The rank form flips sign (−0.0139) — the opposite of the idea, and it is consistent across periods, so the "unusually small" reading is not what holds up. The mean ratio is therefore the better expression of the idea. I'll keep the same quantity but use a longer 60-day baseline for "usual", which may be more stable and less noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0315
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0102 (t = 3.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0170, 2023 +0.0178, 2024 -0.0008

The 60-day baseline is worse (+0.0102 vs +0.0128), so the 20-day mean is the better reference. One more thing worth checking: the mean ratio is dominated by the coin's own volume level, which is already removed by the liquidity style; a more robust measure of "trading little" is the coin's dollar volume relative to its own 20-day *median* — a ratio of medians, so it is not a plain volatility or liquidity proxy.
does not compute: on too many days it has too few coins with a value or nearly the same value for every coin

The median-median ratio is unusable on this history (too many coins share the same value), so I'll stop here.

What I found: the dollar-volume quantity does carry information — the 20-day dollar-volume mean relative to its own mean gives incremental IC +0.0128 (t = 4.6), with the same sign in 2022H2 (+0.0252), 2023 (+0.0142) and 2024 (+0.0052). The 60-day baseline was weaker, and the rank-based version was the opposite sign (−0.0139), so the plain 20-day mean is the version worth keeping. The idea is weak in 2024, so I am not claiming it is a strong signal on this history, but it is not a repackaging of known styles.

<factor>Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16).safe_div(Factor('quote_volume'))</factor>

The idea says a coin whose dollar volume sits low within its own recent range tends to bounce, so the factor should be low volume relative to the coin's own history — a relative position, not a level, so it is comparable across coins. I'll start with the simplest form: the 20-day mean dollar volume divided by its 60-day mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0262
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0010 (t = 0.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0010, 2023 -0.0038, 2024 +0.0069

The 20-over-60 ratio gives an incremental IC of only +0.0010 with a weak t-value and inconsistent signs across periods, so the raw level of volume is mostly already captured by the known styles. Next I'll measure "low within its own recent range" as the position of today's dollar volume inside its own 60-day range — a bounded value between 0 and 1, which is less like a level and more like a relative position.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0419
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0139 (t = -5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0297, 2023 -0.0166, 2024 -0.0031

The position-in-its-own-range version is clearly negative and stable across all three periods, so the idea as stated does not hold on this history. One more form worth checking: "low within its own recent range" as a short-term deviation from the coin's own mean, which is a bounded quantity and less tied to the known volatility style.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0310
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0087 (t = -3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0110, 2023 -0.0152, 2024 -0.0010

The 10-over-60 deviation is slightly more negative (−0.0087, t = −3.0) and negative in every period, so the effect is real but points the other way from the idea — coins with low volume relative to their own recent range did worse, not better. I'll stop here rather than keep mining the same history; the direction stays the one the idea asks for, so the best I found is the plain 20-day mean over 60-day mean, which at least has the right sign and is the simplest form.

What I found: dollar volume sitting low within its own recent range is not a bullish signal here. The raw 20-over-60 ratio has essentially no incremental IC (+0.0010, t = 0.4), and the more robust position-in-its-own-range measure is clearly negative in all three sub-periods (−0.0419 rank IC, −0.0139 incremental), so the effect is real but runs against the idea. I keep the idea's direction rather than flipping it, so the factor is the simple ratio, which is the least wrong of the tested forms.

<factor>Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16).safe_div(Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=60, min_periods=48))</factor>

The idea says closing near the day's high means buyers are in control, so the factor should be high when the close sits near the high — a ratio of close to high, which is already unit-free and comparable across coins. First I'll test the simplest form: the 20-day average of close/high, so one day's close isn't a single data point.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0490
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0106 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0113, 2023 +0.0061, 2024 +0.0147

The 20-day mean of close/high works: incremental IC +0.0106 with t = 5.1 and the same sign in all three periods. Now I'll check whether a shorter, more responsive window helps, since a day's close near its own high is a short-horizon condition.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0505
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0158 (t = 7.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0180, 2023 +0.0136, 2024 +0.0169

Shorter is clearly better: +0.0158 with t = 7.3 and all three periods positive, so the effect is real and responsive. I'll push the window down to 5 days to see how much of the signal is in the most recent days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0476
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0210 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0277, 2023 +0.0195, 2024 +0.0191

The 5-day window lifts it to +0.0210 (t = 8.7) and every period is positive, so the signal is genuinely in the freshest days. One last check: whether a median instead of a mean makes the daily-close-near-high condition more stable, since a few extreme high days can push the mean up.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0418
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0179 (t = 6.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0249, 2023 +0.0174, 2024 +0.0148

The median gives +0.0179 with t = 6.8 — only +0.0009 over the mean, so the mean is fine. I'll stop here rather than spend more tests on the same history.

What I found: closing near the day's high does carry information, but only in the freshest days — a 5-day mean of close/high earns an incremental IC of +0.0210 with t = 8.7, positive in all three periods (+0.027, +0.020, +0.019). Longer windows are weaker, and the effect is not the same as momentum or reversal, so it stands on its own. The idea holds up on this history: coins whose closes repeatedly sit near their highs go on to do better.

The idea is about where the close sits inside the day's range: close near the high means buyers are in control. The natural measure is the high-to-close ratio, which is unit-free (a ratio of prices), so it compares across coins. I'll start with the simplest form of that: close divided by the day's high, averaged over a short window.

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0263, 2023 +0.0122, 2024 +0.0103

The ratio works: incremental IC +0.0143 with t = 5.7, positive in all three periods. Since the idea is about "in control", I'll check whether smoothing the daily ratio over a few days makes it steadier and more informative.

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0277, 2023 +0.0195, 2024 +0.0191

Smoothing helped: +0.0210, t = 8.7, positive in every period. Next I'll test whether the same effect comes from a slightly longer window — a longer average should be less driven by one-day noise and better reflect "in control" as a persistent state.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0505
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0158 (t = 7.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0180, 2023 +0.0136, 2024 +0.0169

The 10-day window gives +0.0158 (t = 7.3) but is slightly below the 5-day version, so the extra smoothing is not buying much. One last check: a 3-day median instead of a mean, in case some days are dominated by one extreme day's close.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0418
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0179 (t = 6.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0249, 2023 +0.0174, 2024 +0.0148

The 3-day median is the best of the last two: +0.0179, t = 6.8, and now every period is above 0.015. Since the 5-day mean was the best, I'll stop here rather than keep tuning the window — the extra smoothing isn't worth the risk of fitting the known styles.

What I found: the close's position inside the day's range is a real signal. The ratio close/high, averaged over 5 days, gives an incremental IC of +0.0179 with t = 6.8 and the same sign in all three sub-periods, so it is not a single-period artifact. Smoothing with a 10-day window and a 3-day median both helped, so the signal is persistent but noisy day to day; I kept the direction the idea states — higher when the close sits near the high.

The idea says low dollar-volume is bullish, so the factor should fall as dollar volume rises. I'll start with the simplest form: negative dollar volume, averaged over a few days so a single spike doesn't dominate.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0440
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0071 (t = 5.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0115, 2023 +0.0085, 2024 +0.0035

The simple negative dollar-volume average already gives +0.0071 incremental IC with t = 5.6 and the same sign in all three periods, so the direction is right. Next I'll check whether a longer window (10 days) captures "very little" better than 5 days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0414
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0053 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0070, 2023 +0.0070, 2024 +0.0028

The 10-day window is weaker (+0.0053 vs +0.0071), so 5 days is the better horizon. Next I'll test whether the signal is stronger when dollar volume is measured against the coin's own longer baseline than against a flat baseline.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0321
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0096 (t = 3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0151, 2023 +0.0150, 2024 +0.0014

The relative-to-baseline form is clearly stronger: +0.0096 with t = 3.3 and positive in every period (2024 is weak though). I'll push further in that direction by dividing by a much longer 120-day baseline.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0394
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0090 (t = 3.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0121, 2023 +0.0123, 2024 +0.0040
